meta.about_government_approval: The US federal government does not approve halal certifiers, and USDA FSIS does not define what is halal. Some states regulate halal claims; New York has certifiers file with its Department of Agriculture and Markets, shown here as 'NYSDAM'. The other recognitions are by foreign halal authorities (Malaysia's JAKIM, Indonesia's BPJPH).
meta.red_meat_note: In the US, machine slaughter is used only for poultry, so beef, lamb and goat are cut by hand. Where a certifier publishes nothing species-specific, red-meat hand slaughter is recorded with basis 'industry_practice'.
meta.poultry_note: Most large US halal poultry plants use a mechanical blade after stunning. 'Zabiha' has no legal definition in the US, so it does not guarantee hand slaughter; check the certifier.
meta.disclaimer: Compiled from public sources on the date above. Several US certifiers publish no written slaughter or stunning standard; 'unknown' means no reliable public source was found. Confirm with the certifier before relying on any field.
